previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and chronic gastroparesis was admitted for worsening abdominal pain and nausea, consistent with a gastroparesis flare triggered by back pain and anxiety. She presented with severe pain and dehydration, requiring IV fluids and pain control. Her symptoms improved with treatment, and she was able to tolerate a full diet by discharge. Labs showed elevated creatinine at 2.0, which decreased to 1.8 but remained concerning for possible progression of diabetic nephropathy. Lisinopril was discontinued due to kidney concerns, and amlodipine was started for blood pressure management. Sinus tachycardia, likely due to pain and anxiety, improved with symptom control. She was discharged home with plans for nephrology follow-up and continuation of her diabetes and psychiatric medications.
